ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy 997d9970c437 (2026-05-05T08:45:37Z) bumped the go-production-dependencies group and modified src/frontend/rpc/product_catalog.go. The change introduced a streaming gRPC client call to ProductCatalogService/SearchProducts without properly handling client-side context cancellation: when the HTTP client disconnects, the goroutine blocked on stream.RecvMsg() is never unblocked because the parent context is not propagated to the gRPC stream and stream.CloseSend() is never called. This causes one goroutine to leak per disconnecting client. Under moderate traffic (~300 req/s with typical early-disconnect rate), goroutines accumulate faster than GC can reclaim associated memory, leading to goroutine count exceeding 50k and OOMKill within ~4 minutes of sustained load.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately restart the frontend pod to restore service (kubectl rollout restart deployment/frontend -n otel-demo). 2. Roll back to the previous frontend image (pre-997d9970c437) using kubectl rollout undo deployment/frontend -n otel-demo to prevent recurrence on restart. 3. Fix src/frontend/rpc/product_catalog.go: pass the HTTP request context to grpc.NewStream(), call stream.CloseSend() in a deferred function upon handler return, and add a goroutine that calls stream.Cancel() when the HTTP request context is Done(). 4. Add a goroutine-count metric alert at threshold 5000 for earlier detection. 5. Deploy the fixed version after code review and regression testing.
